taxonomic_note: Accepted Tragia betonicifolia Nutt. Preserve the nomenclatural warning that the later illegitimate homonym Tragia betonicifolia (Klotzsch) Müll.Arg. is a different South American taxon now treated as Tragia leucandra.
look_here_first: Start with the leaf base and male-flower pedicels: triangular-lanceolate to triangular-ovate serrate leaves with truncate-to-cordate bases; staminate flowers are clustered distally and their persistent pedicel bases are very short.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Deep Review A locked Hays, Travis, Kerr, and Gillespie from USDA-derived county distribution; Hays + Travis + Kerr are retained as the three-count project PASS set.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not infer counties from statewide Texas range or from the source-pool Hays-local flag alone.

best_field_traits: perennial herb or subshrub with stinging hairs
persistent staminate pedicel bases about 0.3–0.6 mm
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Short persistent staminate pedicel bases and distally clustered male flowers are especially useful; T. urticifolia has longer staminate pedicels and a different distribution of staminate flowers.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Short persistent staminate pedicel bases and distally clustered male flowers are especially useful; T. urticifolia has longer staminate pedicels and a different distribution of staminate flowers.
